title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside a long section on notation for the categories built from an additive category A: A^· (cochain complexes), A_· (chain complexes), A_* (simplicial objects), A^* (cosimplicial objects), and mixed iterates such as A_*^·. Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe equivalences, e.g. σ : (A_*)^· ≅ (A^·)_*, identify these categories with one another.

1. End of the previous paragraph. A mixed chain–cochain bicomplex K^·_· has a total complex with terms in both positive and negative degrees. One would need a convention saying whether total degree favours the cochain index or the chain index. Grothendieck explicitly leaves this open: "Je n'ai pas encore vu le besoin urgent d'une telle convention de notations."

2. Duality. Given an anti-equivalence ∨ : A ≅ B°, the index notation is dualized index by index: upper indices become lower and lower become upper. For example (K_*^·)^∨ = K^*_·. Dualizing a simplicial object of cochain complexes gives a cosimplicial object of chain complexes in B. In the list (K) of mixed categories on the previous page, the categories corresponding under duality are to be written one below the other.

3. Sign remark. Bicomplexes of cochains (objects of A^{··}) are defined as complexes of complexes, so the two differentials d', d'' commute. This is not the Cartan–Eilenberg convention of anticommuting differentials. Consequently a sign must be inserted in the total differential, e.g. d = d' + (−1)^p d''. This keeps the iterated-category formalism (A^·)^· strictly compositional.

4. Transition to Prop. 2 on the next page. The text returns to page 1's theme of "invariants associated to X_* ∈ Ob Ss" and the "topos de Dold-Puppe", meaning the simplicial-set topos Ss = Δ^ viewed together with the Dold–Puppe correspondence.
- Prop. 2(a): colimit-commuting functors Ss → A amount, by Kan extension along Yoneda, to cosimplicial objects of A. By dual Dold–Kan these are cochain complexes A^·.
- Prop. 2(b): limit-commuting functors Ss° → B amount to simplicial objects of B, hence to chain complexes B_·.
- Concretely F_K(X) = Hom(C_·(X), K_·), where C_·(X) is the normalized chain complex of Z(X).
- So C_·(X) is the 'universal additive invariant' of X, and such functors are exactly the representable functors on chain complexes.

The purpose is to set up a coherent notational and conceptual framework for the divided-power de Rham complex lectures, where simplicial, cosimplicial and complex structures are mixed constantly.
errors: No mathematical error. The total-degree convention for mixed bicomplexes is deliberately left unfixed.

Prop. 2(a), on the next page, needs A cocomplete and idempotent-complete (Karoubian) for the colimit extension and Dold–Kan to apply; 'additives' alone is not quite enough. (b) needs the dual hypotheses (complete and Karoubian) on B. This is a gap in the stated hypotheses only.

ideas.what: Extending index-position notation (upper/lower, simplicial */complex ·) through a duality A ≅ B° by swapping all index positions
ideas.modern_name: Notational convention for duals of (co)simplicial complexes

ideas.what: Bicomplexes as complexes of complexes with commuting differentials, with a sign put in the total differential (not the Cartan–Eilenberg anticommuting convention)
ideas.modern_name: Commuting-square convention for double complexes; Koszul sign in Tot

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors from simplicial sets to A correspond to cosimplicial objects, hence to cochain complexes via Dold–Kan; C_·(X) is the universal additive invariant
ideas.modern_name: Nerve/realization (Kan extension) plus Dold–Kan; linearization Z[X]

deep.surprise_reason: The page is about notational and sign conventions plus a transition to a standard Kan-extension/Dold–Kan statement. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The first line reads roughly 'qui donne la préférence [struck word] aux cochaînes ou aux chaînes'. The '(9)' is the page number, not part of the text.
'Dans la suite d'objets variables[?] [-(?)-]' should be 'Dans la suite d'objets notés/écrits (K) de la page précédente'. This refers to the list labelled (K) on the previous page.
'd'' et d''[?]' should read d' et d''.
'associés à des X_α et des F[?]' should read 'associés à des X_* ∈ Ob Ss'.
'Il faudra donc un signe : la diff. totale' is more likely 'un signe dans (or à) la diff. totale'.
